My story

Passion, craft
& flavour.

I'm Nigar Parvin — Chef de Partie at Stoke Place Hotel, Slough. MSc graduate, award-winning chef, and passionate creator of flavour-first cooking. My journey began in 2021 and every kitchen since has shaped who I am.

4+
Years experience
3🥈
Award medals
5
Kitchens
🏆 Craft Guild · UK Curry Championship
🥈 Silver — Street Food
🥉 Bronze — Dessert
🥉 Bronze — UK Curry Championship Finale

Who I am

A chef shaped
by curiosity.

I hold a Master's in Data Science & Analytics from Royal Holloway, University of London — a background that gives me a unique analytical edge in the kitchen, from precise recipe development to understanding flavour science.

But my true calling has always been food. Since 2021, I've worked my way through some incredible kitchens — from learning the fundamentals as a commis chef, to working alongside celebrity chef Giancarlo Caldesi at his AA Rosette restaurant in Bray.

I thrive under pressure, care deeply about hygiene and food safety, and believe the best dishes are born from both technique and heart. I'm flexible, confident, and always ready to grow.

MSc Data Science & Analytics Level 2 Food Safety Food Allergy & Intolerance Menu Planning

Signature Dish

Scallops with Cauliflower
Purée & Dill Oil

A refined dish that balances the delicate sweetness of seared scallops with a velvety cauliflower purée and a vibrant fresh dill oil. Elegant, clean, and deeply satisfying.

3
Scallops
45
Mins
2
Servings

Ingredients

Cauliflower Purée

  • 1 small cauliflower
  • 2 cups water
  • 2 cups milk
  • 2 cups double cream
  • 1 tbsp salt
  • 1 tbsp pepper
  • 2g thyme
  • 20g butter

Dill Oil

  • 100g fresh dill
  • 200ml cold-pressed rapeseed oil
  • 1 tbsp salt

Scallops

  • 3 scallops
  • 1 tbsp butter
  • Salt & pepper

🌿 Dairy Free Option

Boil cauliflower with water or oat milk, season, and blend with margarine instead of butter.

Method

1

Make the Cauliflower Purée

In a deep pan, combine water, milk, and double cream. Bring to a boil, then add chopped cauliflower, salt, pepper, and thyme. Cook until the cauliflower is completely soft. Drain through a strainer, transfer to a blender with 20g butter, and blend until silky smooth.

2

Make the Dill Oil

Blanch 100g fresh dill in salted boiling water for 10 seconds, then immediately plunge into ice water. Drain thoroughly, blend with 200ml cold-pressed rapeseed oil until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve or muslin cloth into a squeeze bottle and refrigerate.

3

Sear the Scallops

Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Season scallops with salt and pepper. Place in the pan with space between each one. Cook 2 minutes without moving. When deep golden on the bottom, flip and cook 1 minute 30 seconds. Add butter, baste for 30 seconds. Do not overcook — they should be just set.

4

Plate & Serve

Spoon a generous swipe of cauliflower purée onto a warm plate. Place the seared scallops on top. Drizzle the vibrant dill oil around the plate. Garnish with crispy bacon if using. Serve immediately.

Signature Dish

Chicken Meatballs in
Rich White Gravy

Tender steamed and golden chicken meatballs nestled in a smooth, aromatic cashew and cream gravy. Inspired by South Asian flavours, adapted for any table. Perfect with rice, naan, or pasta.

250g
Chicken Mince
60
Mins
3–4
Servings

Ingredients

Meatballs

  • 250g chicken mince
  • 3 tbsp plain flour
  • 1 tbsp black pepper
  • Salt to taste

White Gravy

  • ½ tsp whole cumin & coriander
  • ¼ tsp cinnamon powder
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 7 cashew nuts (or 10g pine nuts)
  • 2 tbsp double cream
  • 2 medium onions
  • 1 tbsp fenugreek leaf
  • 1 green chilli (optional)
  • 1 tomato
  • 1 clove garlic, 2g ginger
  • Salt & black pepper
  • 1 tbsp ghee or butter

🌿 Allergen Options

  • Gluten free: Use 2 eggs instead of flour
  • Nut free: Use pine nuts or extra cream
  • Dairy free: Swap cream for almond milk
  • Egg & gluten free: Skip both — steam only, they bind naturally

Method

1

Make & Steam the Meatballs

Mix chicken mince, flour, pepper and salt until well combined. Shape into 18g mini meatballs. Steam for 20 minutes, then allow to cool. Reserve the drained steaming water — it adds flavour to the gravy.

2

Lightly Fry the Meatballs

Deep fry the cooled meatballs until just light golden — you don't want a dark crust, just a gentle colour. Drain and set aside.

3

Build the Gravy

Heat 3 tbsp oil in a pan. Add whole spices and nuts, stir 1 minute. Add garlic, ginger, onion and chilli. Caramelise on medium-low heat. Add tomato, cook until soft. Add 1 cup water and simmer 1 minute. Cool, then blend completely smooth. Strain for a silky texture.

4

Finish & Serve

Melt ghee or butter in a pan, add the strained gravy. Season with salt and pepper. If too thick, add reserved steaming water. Stir in double cream and crushed fenugreek. Add meatballs and cook 2 minutes. Garnish with parsley and coriander. Serve with rice, naan, or pasta. ✨ Add saffron to the meatballs or rice for extra luxury.

Signature Dish

Pan-Fried Salmon with
Lemon Caper Butter Sauce

Crispy-skinned salmon finished in the oven, served with a bright, tangy lemon caper butter sauce. A restaurant-quality dish ready in under 30 minutes — alcohol-free and full of flavour.

1
Salmon Fillet
25
Mins
1
Serving

Ingredients

Salmon

  • 1 salmon fillet
  • 4g thyme
  • 1 garlic clove
  • 2 tbsp oil
  • 15g butter
  • Salt & black pepper

Lemon Caper Butter Sauce

  • ½ shallot, finely chopped
  • 1 small garlic clove, chopped
  • ¼ red chilli, chopped
  • 1 tbsp capers
  • 1 lemon — juice & zest
  • 30g butter
  • ¼ tsp plain flour (for thickness)
  • 1 tsp oil
  • ¼ tsp chopped parsley
  • Salt & black pepper

💡 Chef's Tip

Sprinkling sea salt directly in the pan before adding the salmon helps achieve an extra crispy skin without sticking.

Method

1

Make the Lemon Caper Sauce

In a hot pan, heat 1 tsp oil and 30g butter. Add garlic and stir briefly. Add shallots and red chilli, cook until caramelised. Add capers, salt and pepper. Mix well, then add lemon juice. Mix flour with a little water to make a runny paste and stir in — add 3 tbsp hot water to balance. Bring to one boil, remove from heat, stir in chopped parsley.

2

Season the Salmon

Pat the salmon fillet dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides.

3

Pan-Fry for Crispy Skin

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan. Sprinkle sea salt directly in the hot pan, then place the salmon skin-side down on low-medium heat. Add thyme and a garlic clove to the pan. Add 15g butter, let it melt, then baste the top of the fish continuously for 2 minutes.

4

Finish in the Oven

Transfer to a parchment-lined tray, skin-side up. Bake at 180°C for 4 minutes. Plate the salmon, spoon over the warm lemon caper butter sauce generously, and serve immediately.
